verdicts.reason: Neither is shippable. A cuts the dark header down to a stub that covers only the top-left of the canvas, and the headline is jammed right under it. The orange divider is stranded alone at the far right edge, the body copy and legal line are tiny, and the right side is a loose, unbalanced column. B has a stronger banner structure: the dark brand panel with its logo sits on the left and the content on the right. But the orange divider runs through the body copy (over 'and released'), the body block is offset to the right instead of sharing the headline's axis, the logo looks small and lost in the big dark panel, and the legal line can't be read at this size. B is still the better of the two.
